A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TESS 2 research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite revisions and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original diffusion-adaptation, instruction-tuning and analysis results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 2–4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds a second-reward-model comparison in Figure 3a and a qualitative masking-pilot result in Appendix A.1.

M1.justification: UL2 masking, shifted labels, bidirectional attention, cross-entropy training, self-conditioning and reward-gradient guidance are retained. Expanded label-shifting notation and removal of the detailed self-conditioning explanation do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The documented Dolma, C4, Tulu 2/3, preference-data and GSM8k coverage and six downstream benchmarks remain. The added reward-model and masking checks address the existing AlpacaEval setting; no distinct task or domain is introduced.

E2.justification: Figure 3a adds weqweasdas/RM-Mistral-7B as an alternative reward model alongside the authors' trained model. Table 3's downstream baselines remain unchanged. LLaDA is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: The added reward-model comparison varies the reward checkpoint. Appendix A.1 newly reports a control omitting aggressive T5 masking, using different but unspecified pilot data and hyperparameters. Retained benchmark splits, metrics, inference budgets and timing settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds evidence about sensitivity to reward-model choice and reports that removing aggressive T5 masking hurt AlpacaEval performance in an earlier pilot. Existing base-model, adaptation-duration, diffusion-step and generation analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests for these results. The added reward-model curve retains point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 3a adds an off-the-shelf reward-model curve with a reported AlpacaEval gain of about four points over no guidance, alongside the retained roughly three-point trained-model gain. Appendix A.1 adds qualitative masking underperformance. Tables 1–3 and the 480-versus-77-second timing result are unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix E derives autoregressive and diffusion generation-cost expressions and asserts that B < L + 1 implies lower diffusion cost. This mathematical analysis is absent from v1. The expanded label-shifting notation explains the existing procedure.

C1.justification: The main adaptation, performance, reward-guidance and inference-compute claims remain. Introduction contribution 2 drops the explicit recommendation for a bidirectionally pretrained base model and instead emphasizes base-model choice generally.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation that guidance generalizes across reward models and expands the mathematical-data-quality explanation of reasoning failures. Its speed limitations omit v1's explicit warning that optimized AR inference such as vLLM can dramatically reduce AR runtime.

D1.justification: v2 identifies and links the additional reward checkpoint and open-instruct training recipe. It removes the explicit self-conditioning procedure, probability-averaging formula and training/inference probabilities of 0.5/1, while retaining self-conditioning by reference. This is reduced documentation, not evidence of changed settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds LLaDA and contrasts its training from scratch with TESS 2's adaptation approach, and adds OLMo 2 to the data-quality discussion. It also removes the assertion that Han et al. (2024a) pretrain their own AR and diffusion models.

P1.justification: Local wording edits and expanded label-shifting explanation accompany removal of the self-conditioning subsection. The timing discussion moves from Limitations to new Section 5.4, and new Appendix E shifts the former Appendices E–G to F–H. The overall narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3a gains a second curve, a legend and an expanded vertical range. Tables 1–2 and Figure 2 are repositioned with text reflow. Appendix Figures 4–6 and their example-generation pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: The second-reward-model check adds useful robustness evidence, but v2 loses explicit self-conditioning details and weakens the optimized-AR caveat. New Appendix E also introduces a cost condition contradicted by its own formulas: B=L>1 satisfies B<L+1 yet gives higher diffusion cost. These losses in reproducibility and mathematical rigor outweigh the limited added evidence, while the central experimental results remain intact.
